The evidence presented in the text involves financial statements submitted by the plaintiff in the case *Green vs. National Bank*. The credibility of this evidence is significantly undermined because the documents are photocopies rather than originals. In legal proceedings, the authenticity of documentary evidence is crucial, and the absence of original copies for verification, especially when contested by the opposing party (the bank), raises serious doubts about the reliability and admissibility of the financial statements. Therefore, the evidence is currently of low credibility due to the inability to verify its authenticity.
